body.statement: At \(q=q^\star\), the explicit estimator \(\delta_{n,q^\star}\) satisfies \[\max_{z\in\mathcal T^n}R_n(\mathcal D_{q^\star},\delta_{n,q^\star};z)\le n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\] uniformly over complete schedules. The explicit prior \(\Pi_n\) satisfies, uniformly over every schedule-independent \(\mathcal D\), \[\inf_{\widehat\tau}\mathbb E_{z\sim\Pi_n}R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)\ge n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).\] The broad component yields a positive quadratic coercivity term in \(\|\bar q(\mathcal D)-q^\star\|\); completing the square against the linear half-effect-prior term contributes only \(o(n^{-4/3})\). Finally, with \(M=n\), both rational grid programs bracket their continuous orbit games within \(1/(4n^2)=o(n^{-4/3})\).
body.proof_tex:
First consider the iid design \(q^\star\).  Since \(c_a/q_a^\star=2\operatorname{sign}(c_a)\), write
\[
T_{n,q^\star}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n W_i,\qquad
W_i=\operatorname{sign}(c_{A_i})(2Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1)\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
For a fixed schedule the \(W_i\) are independent,
\[
\mathbb EW_i=\mu(t_i),\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(T_{n,q^\star})
=\frac1n-\frac1{n^2}\sum_i\mu(t_i)^2.
\tag{13}
\]
Put \(Q=\sum_i\mu(t_i)^2\), \(A_n=Q/n^{2/3}\), \(x=n^{1/3}\tau(z)\), and \(\varepsilon=T_{n,q^\star}-\tau(z)\).  Bounded independence gives \(\mathbb E|\varepsilon|^3=O(n^{-3/2})\), uniformly in \(z\).  The regularity of \(s_3\) permits Taylor expansion of the two cross terms in the squared risk, uniformly in \(x\), and yields
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[
\varepsilon-n^{-2/3}s_3\{x+n^{1/3}\varepsilon\}
\right]^2
=\frac1n+n^{-4/3}
\left[-A_n-2(1-Q/n)s_3'(x)+s_3(x)^2\right]
+O(n^{-3/2}).
\tag{14}
\]
Indeed, the cross-term remainder is bounded by a constant times
\(n^{-2/3}n^{2/3}\mathbb E|\varepsilon|^3=O(n^{-3/2})\), and the last-square remainder has the same or smaller order because \(s_3^2\) is Lipschitz.

Every response type satisfies \(\mu(t)^2\geq|\mu(t)|/2\), so
\[
A_n\geq\frac{|x|}{2},\qquad 0\leq A_n\leq n^{1/3}.
\tag{15}
\]
The Riccati identity changes the bracket in (14) to
\[
-A_n+\frac{|x|}{2}-C_3+2n^{-1/3}A_ns_3'(x).
\tag{16}
\]
For large \(n\), boundedness of \(s_3'\) makes (16) decreasing in \(A_n\).  Its maximum under (15) is therefore attained at \(A_n=|x|/2\), and
\[
n^{-1/3}|x|\,|s_3'(x)|
\leq K n^{-1/3}|x|(1+|x|)^{-1/2}
=O(n^{-1/6}),
\]
because \(|x|\leq n^{1/3}\).  Projection onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase squared distance from \(\tau(z)\in[-1,1]\).  Equations (14)--(16) prove the asserted uniform upper bound.

For the lower construction, the label-preserving expansion gives, for the half-effect prior,
\[
B_{A,n}(\mathcal D)\geq
\frac1n-n^{-4/3}
\left[I(f)+\frac12m_1(f)+2m_1(f)
\{\bar q_1(\mathcal D)-1/2\}\right]
+O_f(n^{-5/3}).
\tag{17}
\]
The broad-prior lemma gives
\[
B_{B,n}(\mathcal D)\geq
\frac{1+k\|\bar q(\mathcal D)-q^\star\|^2}{n}
-Kn^{-9/8}.
\tag{18}
\]
Bayes risk is concave in the prior: the infimum of a mixture of risk functionals is at least the same mixture of their infima.  With \(\gamma_n=n^{-1/4}\), (17)--(18) therefore imply, writing \(d=\bar q(\mathcal D)-q^\star\),
\[
B_{\Pi_n}(\mathcal D)\geq
\frac1n-\{I(f)+m_1(f)/2\}n^{-4/3}
+k n^{-5/4}\|d\|^2
-2m_1(f)n^{-4/3}d_1
-O_f(n^{-11/8})-O_f(n^{-5/3}).
\tag{19}
\]
Completing the square gives
\[
k n^{-5/4}\|d\|^2-2m_1(f)n^{-4/3}d_1
\geq-\frac{m_1(f)^2}{k}n^{-17/12}
=o(n^{-4/3}).
\tag{20}
\]
Choose smooth compactly supported even densities obtained by slowly cutting off and smoothing \(\phi_3^2\).  The Airy variational identity gives
\[
I(f)+\frac12m_1(f)\longrightarrow C_3.
\]
A diagonal cutoff sequence makes its approximation error and all remainders in (19) \(o(n^{-4/3})\), uniformly in \(\mathcal D\).  Equations (19)--(20) prove the stated all-design Bayes lower bound for the explicit complete-schedule mixture.

Finally, the grid-randomization lemma with \(M=n\) gives
\[
0\leq\Lambda_{n,n}^{\mathrm{all}}-G_n^{\mathrm{all}}
\leq\frac1{4n^2},\qquad
0\leq\Lambda_{n,n}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)-G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)
\leq\frac1{4n^2}.
\]
Since \(n^{-2}=o(n^{-4/3})\), these are the claimed rational finite-game brackets.
body.justification: The proposition makes the asymptotic saddle operational and prevents the sharp value from resting on an unattained formal operator.
body.gap: The two-arm paper constructs a scalar feedback rule and scalar Airy-squared priors; the proposed constructions must preserve arm labels and regularize every dependent assignment law without changing the second-order coefficient.
body.consumer: The estimator is directly implementable under iid \(q^\star\), while the rational certificates allow exact finite-sample auditing of its worst-case risk.
